definition: Gravity Battery Towers: towers storing energy as lifted mass.

t: Real Research Today: Gravity Battery Towers
title: Real Research Today: Gravity Battery Towers
definition: Today's documented research behind Gravity Battery Towers.
description:
The road to Gravity Battery Towers is already being paved. Green hydrogen electrolyzer capacity is scaling under EU and US clean-hydrogen programs. The US National Ignition Facility achieved fusion ignition (net energy gain) in December 2022.

Perovskite solar cells have passed 33% tandem efficiency in laboratory records. Together these programs form the weight blocks foundation that Gravity Battery Towers will build on — the tower logistics results, the crane systems methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as tower logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2032 — First commercial tower hulls plant sells weight blocks power to
definition: 2032 milestone on the Gravity Battery Towers roadmap.
description:
First commercial tower hulls plant sells weight blocks power to the grid under a 20-year round-trip efficiency contract.

What must be true first: the weight blocks results have to replicate outside the lab, tower logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and crane systems operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed weight blocks demonstrations, tower logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting crane systems uptime. When all three flash green, 2032 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (6 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Gravity Battery Towers
definition: Estimates Gravity Battery Towers readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Gravity Battery Towers components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a tower hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Gravity Battery Towers Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Gravity Battery Towers operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Gravity Battery Towers installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 46544 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where weight blocks monitoring, tower logistics redundancy, or crane systems maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Gravity Battery Towers Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Gravity Battery Towers: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Gravity Battery Towers — towers storing energy as lifted mass.

Phase 1 — Prove (weight blocks): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (tower logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (crane systems): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (round-trip efficiency): tower hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and grids-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
